correctness.rationale: The displacement normal-ordering identity is independently checked against physical-space integrals. Every angular mode is a Laguerre polynomial of precisely controlled degree; divisibility by the product of distinct squared radii, with an extra zero from known trace, reconstructs the full rank and all boundary cases. A nonzero kernel perturbation of the maximally mixed state yields distinct strictly positive density matrices. Antipodal conjugacy and finite Fourier interpolation prove the angular count. Seventy-two exact rational-rank checks and 45 quadratures support, but do not replace, the symbolic argument.

value.rationale: A Weyl characteristic function can be measured directly. The theorem gives a completely sharp universal measurement design: any N positive distinct rings suffice for an N-level cutoff, fewer always fail on positive states, and a perfect-square nullity measures exactly how much information is lost. A finite sharp per-ring angular grid replaces continuum traces. These are motivated information-completeness and experimental-sampling questions rather than unmotivated arithmetic slices; no noise-optimality or global point-count claim is made.
